position.name: The Field
position.sceneSentence: A capture-first person opens the app mid-thought to shoot a bill, an idea, or a to-do down before it is gone, and needs to see their entire mental field present and actionable at a glance.
position.oneParagraph: The Field is a bento board of your whole brain. Open it and everything you are carrying is already there: bills, ideas, to-dos, events, somedays, each in its own soft-tinted tile, color-coded and packed with the real, tappable items rather than a count to click through. A warm Fraunces serif headline greets you like a person, not a dashboard. Capture lives in an always-on clay bar pinned to the bottom, one tap from any screen. The system is built for an ADHD glance: out of sight is out of mind, so nothing is hidden behind a filter, and nothing on screen is a dead label. It is bold the way an editorial page is bold, through confident type and a disciplined pastel system that survives both light and dark, never through gradients, badges, or decoration. The New Yorker organizing your life: warm, graphic, and unmistakably not a productivity template.
position.feelInFirst3Seconds: Everything I am carrying is right here, and I can act on any of it without hunting. Warm, graspable, mine.
position.wouldBeWrongToFeel: Curated-down, filtered, performative, or like another cheerful productivity app with streaks and badges.

references.lesson: Desaturated pastel category cards (powder blue, peach, sage, blush, lavender, butter) with ink-line icons and serif labels read beautifully in both light and dark mode. Pastels become the entry-type color system.

references.ref: The New Yorker (issue table of contents)
references.lesson: Tiny all-caps kicker over a serif headline gives editorial reverence to content. The kicker becomes each tile's color-coded type label.
An editorial serif header and soft warm personality make a planner feel human, not corporate.
Color owning a zone (a drenched header block) is bolder than tinting everything evenly. Informs the saturated kicker and edge-bar carrying the type color while the tile body stays soft.
Large serif on warm cream is bold through scale, not decoration. Informs the Fraunces home headline.

rejectedDirections.name: The Almanac
rejectedDirections.whyRejected: Most elegant/editorial, but a single sectioned feed scrolls; The Field's spatial bento is more 'everything at a glance' and more ADHD-friendly, which the user prioritized.

rejectedDirections.name: The Margin
rejectedDirections.whyRejected: Beautiful risograph-quiet direction, but its generous spacing fights the user's hard requirement that everything be present and actionable at once.

tokens.name: EntryAccent.today
tokens.why: Folded into headline + tile ordering, not a color.

family.why: Fraunces is a warm, characterful old-style serif that delivers the human, non-corporate voice at the top of home; Inter keeps the dense tile content legible and fast. Hierarchy reads as serif-vs-sans plus size.

scale.name: kicker
scale.use: All-caps type label on each tile (Inter, +0.6 tracking)

type.why: The serif/sans split does the heavy lifting so color can stay calm; the kicker is the only all-caps element and carries the type code.

spacing.why: Keep the 4pt base (current code is already 4pt-based, only 43% fit). Enforcing this rhythm fixes the off-beat 3px/14px values the forensics flagged. Vary by zone: tighter inside tiles, generous between sections.

radius.why: Large soft radii make tiles feel like cards you could pick up — graphic and tactile. Replaces the current sharp 4/6px corner language the forensics called 'sharp'.

motion.why: Tiles spring in subtly on open (Reanimated withSpring damping ~16) to feel alive on ProMotion; everything respects useReducedMotion. Transform/opacity only.

scale.name: tile
scale.shadow: warm soft: rgba(80,50,30,0.10), y8, blur20 (ios) / elevation 2 (android)

scale.name: capture
scale.shadow: warm soft: rgba(80,50,30,0.16), y-2, blur16 (ios) / elevation 8 (android)

elevation.why: Gentle warm-tinted lift per tile gives the bento depth without borders; no pure-black shadows.

ruledOut: No FAB — capture is an always-on bottom bar
No gradients anywhere (no LinearGradient buttons or glows)
No pure white (#FFFFFF) or pure black (#000000) — warm extremes only
No 1px structural borders — tonal layering + edge-bars only
No streaks, badges, confetti, or any gamification
No dead count-only tiles — every tile shows real, tappable items
No curating the home down to 'today' — everything stays present and visible
No pastel-illustration mascots or decorative spot art
Kicker is the only all-caps text; no all-caps body or buttons

darkMode.strategy: First-class light AND dark, full parity. Each type has both a light tile-tint and a dark tile-tint of the same hue (dark-adapted lightness) so pastels survive both. Saturated kicker/edge-bar colors are shared across schemes. Resolve via a single useTheme() hook returning the active token set at the provider level — no inline colorScheme ternaries in components.

accessibility.notes: Verify ink-on-tint pairs hit AA in both schemes; saturated kicker text on soft tint must clear 4.5:1. Dynamic Type / font scale to 2x with no fixed-height tiles. Touch targets 44pt iOS / 48dp Android; capture bar and tile items meet minimums.

migrationHints.suggestedNamespace: tokens (replace constants/theme.ts named exports; keep a thin compat shim mapping old names during migration)
migrationHints.dualResidentStrategy: side-by-side until cleanup — introduce new token object alongside existing Surface/TextColors/EntryAccent/Brand exports, migrate screen-by-screen, then delete old exports
migrationHints.phaseHints: Phase 1: land the token object + useTheme() provider and light/dark resolution. Phase 2: build EntryTile (soft tint + kicker + edge-bar + actionable items) and the Fraunces headline; load Fraunces via expo-font before splash. Phase 3: convert home to the bento Field layout and add the always-on capture bar (remove FAB). Phase 4: migrate detail/list/calendar to the new tokens; fix the 418 hardcoded values flagged in forensics; collapse the 6 duplicate color clusters. Phase 5: rewrite PRODUCT.md/DESIGN.md to The Field, then audit on both platforms in both schemes.
